//: Typechecks the test suites, which the shipping tsconfig deliberately excludes.
The suites are plain JavaScript inside `.ts` files on purpose: Node strips the
(absent) annotations and runs them directly, so the project needs no test
toolchain and the tests exercise `src/` rather than a build output. Fixtures
are built by spreading partial literals, which is exactly the idiom a
strict checker rejects even when the tests are sound where it matters.
So this config checks the tests for the errors that actually break them —
typos, missing imports, misuse of the module under test — while leaving the
fixture ergonomics alone. `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` stays on because a test
reading `rows[0].text` unchecked is a test that fails confusingly.
Shipping code under `src/` and `extension/src/` is still checked at full
strictness by tsconfig.json: that is the check guarding the published artifact.
